object_description: two separate structures, a solitary hall building and a residential and service building
geometry_property: oriented to the grain of the surroundings
design_condition: the two structures are carefully positioned along the grain of the surrounding development, forming differentiated outdoor spaces with interesting visual connections and good permeability

positive: Careful positioning of the two structures oriented towards the grain of the surrounding development
The volumes form differentiated outdoor spaces with interesting visual connections and good permeability
The typical green space protrusions and street-side front garden borders are adopted to suit the situation
Both access areas are precisely formulated outdoor spaces with exciting spatial sequences and appropriate permeability
The hall is a solitary building that fits perfectly into the site
The calm continuous height development with perforated sheeting and generous windows lends a modern, distinguished elegance
The external expression communicates the cultural use well
The entrance is carefully balanced, with an inviting forecourt and a view into the foyer
The inner courtyard is appropriately used as a foyer forecourt and is itself enhanced
The routing of visitors is of high quality
The difficult terrain design in the transition to the neighbouring courtyard has been conclusively demonstrated
The foyer is generously dimensioned and spatially attractive
The hall has good spatial proportions in its basic form and with the extension
The window to the outside is a balanced gesture between views in and out and a closed black box
The residential building follows the contour lines and blends naturally into the local architectural structure
The arrangement brings the hall building to the fore and supports its significance as a solitaire with public appeal
The clear separation into two independent buildings gives the municipality all marketing options without financial risk
The apartment layouts suggest a high quality of living
Prime costs are favourable and overall economic viability is positive
The neighbourhood is optimally protected from hall emissions
negative: The row of trees against the streetcar is rather untypical of the neighbourhood and should be questioned
The north-west and north-east facades are not yet satisfactory
The similarity of the window typology to the neighbouring buildings takes away the power of the hall as a solitaire
The finer design and materialisation of hall and foyer is not yet clearly visible
The passage from the stage to the backstage needs to be designed more generously
The principle of following the contour lines is abandoned at one street front
